title: Materialized subagent task file (tasks_schema_version 2)
description: Validates every materialized task file the orchestrators emit — validation_tasks.json, revalidation_tasks.json, consolidation_tasks.json, salvage_task_<model>.json, human_decision_tasks.json and task_generation_tasks.json. Version 1 is the historical reference-based shape that carried no prompt; a reader that finds tasks_schema_version missing or != 2 refuses the file with exit 3 and re-materializes the phase (compatibility policy is regenerate, never upgrade-in-place). This key is deliberately distinct from metadata.schema_version, which versions validation *results*.

tasks_schema_version.description: Integer task-file format version. Missing means 1.

context_contract.description: The validation context contract the file was materialized under (validation/revalidation files). 2 = over-limit documents named by hash-bound snapshot path; missing means 1, whose over-limit prompts were cut at the inline limit and are retired on resume/reaggregate.

kind.description: The kind every task in this file has.

inputs.description: File-level copy of the inputs block; identical to every task's own inputs.

context_plan_file.description: Frozen context-plan snapshot, relative to the phase directory (absolute across drives). Its raw bytes must match inputs.context_plan_sha256 before dispatch.

tasks.description: The task list. Batched kinds carry it under the historical name `batches` instead, so the list is never duplicated on disk; use one accessor (utils.subagent_tasks.tasks_of) rather than guessing.

batches.description: The task list under its historical name, for the batched kinds whose merge and reaggregation paths already read it.

plan_sha256.description: Content hash of the plan file, computed the same way StateManager._compute_plan_hash does (sha256 hexdigest truncated to 16 chars). Empty string when the phase has no plan file.

tasks_sha256.description: Content hash of the task list under review — review-tasks only, whose validation prompts embed the tasks text beside the plan.

diff_base.description: Git ref the diff was taken against (state.head_at_start) — code-review and apply phases only.

diff_sha256.description: Content hash of the diff text — code-review and apply phases only.

reviewed_code_sha256.description: Content hash of the code excerpt the prompts embed — code-review only. Moves when a reviewed file is edited between fan-out and validation, which diff_base alone cannot see.

context_plan_sha256.description: SHA-256 of a commit review's frozen context-plan snapshot, as commit_range.plan_sha256 recorded it — code-review on a commit brief with --context-plan only. A resume or reaggregate whose snapshot no longer hashes to it is refused.

salvage_request_sha256.description: Content hash of the salvage request record — salvage only.

items_sha256.description: Content hash of the judged item set — human_decision_judge only.

task_id.description: Stable, path-free identifier for this task. Named in every refusal message.

prompt.description: The complete prompt. Under context_mode inline it embeds every input the subagent needs; it never names plan_file, grouped_file or output_path.

output_name.description: Bare basename resolved against the phase dir the task file was loaded from.

output_path.description: Derived absolute convenience path for native invokers. Invoker plumbing, never a subagent instruction.

prompt_path.description: Optional absolute path to a sidecar holding exactly the bytes of `prompt` (validation, revalidation, consolidation and task generation only). Invoker plumbing, never a subagent instruction: a host whose subagent tool takes a prompt string may hand the subagent this file instead of re-emitting its prompt (~65 KB for a validation batch, ~21 KB for task generation) through its own context. `prompt` stays the source of truth and every other reader ignores this key.

prompt_lines.description: Line count of `prompt`, and therefore of the sidecar, so a host can tell a subagent to read through the last line rather than trust a default page size.

result_channel.description: Producer intent. Every materialized task is `file`. `inline-json` names only the legacy Claude-Code-interactive shape and is refused before dispatch with exit 3.

context_mode.description: How the task's inputs travel. `inline` embeds content in prompt and runs against any runner. `workspace-read` references absolute paths and requires a runner declaring supports_workspace_reads.

capability_tier.description: Role annotation, never a model. Resolution chain: model_hint (when set and not `auto`) -> capability_tier -> driver.subagent_runner_cheap / driver.subagent_runner -> host default. `cheap` is a permission to downgrade, and the per-kind rules below forbid it wherever AGENTS.md forbids downgrading. No currently materialized kind permits it: `cheap` is reserved for the human-decision fan-out coordinator, a dispatch-only role that writes no verdict and therefore has no task file.

executor_role.description: `agent` means any invoker may dispatch this. `human` means no invoker ever dispatches it; it routes to the human-task pause and the executor refuses it before dispatch (exit 3).

model_hint.description: Free-form model string, or `auto`. Keeps its historical meaning; `full`/`cheap` belong to capability_tier alone and are a schema error here.

subagent_type.description: Optional Claude-Code-only metadata, demoted for one release. No reader branches on it. Must agree with executor_role.

context_sources.description: Validation/revalidation only, and only when some context block is not inline (plans/validation-context-by-path-and-codex-0156-fallout.md §2.3 step 7). One record per context document. A `path` record is the hash-bound snapshot the prompt names by `abs_path`; `path` is relative to the phase dir when the snapshot lives there, so a moved phase dir can rebind it after re-verifying `sha256` (raw bytes). A `truncated` record says why no file is named.

declared_files.description: WRITE kinds only. The file set this batch declares it will touch, repo-root-relative. Drives D3h's pairwise-disjoint co-scheduling admission and D3l's pre-dispatch write-policy check; an EMPTY list means 'undeclared', which runs the task alone rather than being treated as 'touches nothing'.

snapshot_files.description: WRITE kinds only. Files the executor snapshots under {phase}/pre_batch/{task_id}/ before dispatch, so the post-run byte comparison (D3g) and `util restore-batch` (D3l) have a rollback point. Defaults to declared_files when absent.

expected_ids.description: WRITE kinds only. The suggestion/group/task ids this batch is supposed to apply. D3g spot-checks that THESE landed rather than merely that bytes moved: a result reporting only some of them with a non-empty diff is a partial application, not a success.

prior_changes_id.description: WRITE kinds only. The stable `--id` for `prior_changes.py append` (suggestion/group/section/task key — never the loop index), so a re-dispatched batch appends once.

can_parallelize.description: WRITE kinds only. The batcher's opinion that this task may run beside its batch siblings. Necessary but not sufficient: driver.max_concurrent_write_subagents > 1 and the disjointness check must also agree (D3h).

depends_on.description: WRITE kinds only (implement). Task ids this task depends on; the human-task strategies walk these edges (D3n).

is_human.description: WRITE kinds only. Mirror of `executor_role == "human"` for readers that predate D2h. The schema requires the two to agree.

file_key.description: WRITE kinds only (apply_code_fixes). The file a code-fix batch is partitioned by (utils/code_fix_batcher.py). Provenance for the declared file set, never a second source of truth.

task_title.description: WRITE kinds only. Human-readable label for logs, metrics and the implementation summary.
